headline: Debora has had a clear functional decline since the last review: she now needs moderate help with bathing and lower-body dressing and is skipping showers. The record of her Oct 2 fall conflicts with a chart correction, so the team needs to reconcile it.

items.statement: On 2026-10-26 OT found Debora now needs moderate assistance with bathing and lower-body dressing; she was independent at last review. OT recommends a tub transfer bench, handheld shower, and more home care hours for bathing.
items.verifier_note: The 10-26 OT note matches on the new moderate assistance, the prior independence, and all three recommendations.

items.statement: On 2026-10-19 the home care aide reported Debora needed hands-on help getting out of the tub and has been skipping showers because she fears slipping.
items.verifier_note: The 10-19 aide note matches: hands-on help out of the tub, and skipping showers for fear of slipping.

items.statement: The PT evaluation on 2026-10-05 found slow, unsteady gait with intermittent cane use and a Timed Up and Go of 19 seconds. PT recommends a front-wheeled walker, a home safety evaluation, bathroom grab bars, and twice-weekly strength and balance sessions. The note is framed as following a fall on 2026-10-02.
items.verifier_note: The PT note matches on gait, intermittent cane use, TUG of 19 seconds, the recommendations, twice-weekly sessions, and the framing after the 10-02 fall.

items.statement: Documentation conflict: a nursing note dated 2026-10-02 describes a fall at home (skin tear to left forearm, fall risk rated high, PT referral). A 2026-10-04 chart correction says that entry was filed on the wrong participant and should be disregarded. The 2026-10-05 PT note still refers to the fall, so it is unclear whether Debora fell.
items.verifier_note: The 10-02 nursing note, the 10-04 correction saying it was filed on the wrong participant, and the 10-05 PT note that still refers to the fall are all accurately described. The conflict is correctly left unresolved.

items.statement: On 2026-10-13 her spouse and primary caregiver, Kevin, reported exhaustion and poor sleep and worry about managing evenings alone. He asked for respite; respite options and a caregiver support group were discussed. No follow-up is documented in the notes provided.
items.verifier_note: The 10-13 social work note matches on Kevin's exhaustion, poor sleep, evening worry, the respite request, and the options and support group discussed. The cited notes show no follow-up.

items.statement: Sertraline 25 mg was started on 2026-09-13 for depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 of 14), and the pharmacist updated the blister pack on 2026-09-15. A 4-week recheck was planned, but no recheck or repeat PHQ-9 appears in the notes provided.
items.verifier_note: The notes and medication record show sertraline 25 mg started 09-13 with PHQ-9 of 14, the blister pack updated 09-15, and a 4-week recheck planned. The cited notes show no recheck.

items.statement: No influenza vaccine is recorded this season (season began 2026-08-01). The most recent dose was on 2026-04-25.
items.verifier_note: The immunization record shows no flu vaccine this season (season start 2026-08-01) and the latest dose on 2026-04-25.

questions_for_team: Did Debora fall on 2026-10-02? Who will reconcile the nursing note, the chart correction, and the PT note, and confirm the correct fall history and risk level?
How will the team start the OT and PT equipment recommendations (tub transfer bench, handheld shower, walker, grab bars) and the increase in home care hours for bathing?
Has the 4-week sertraline recheck and repeat PHQ-9 happened? If not, who will do it, and should her mood be reviewed in light of her fear of bathing and her reduced function?
What respite and evening support can be offered to Kevin, and who will follow up with him?
Should influenza vaccination be offered this season?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and the last IDT review date, then pull all encounters in the window: ED visits, urgent care, hospital admissions, observation stays, and readmissions, with reasons and discharge summaries.

Falls and injuries: any falls, near-falls, or fall-related injuries in the window, including fracture screening if reported. Check gait, balance, and assistive device use, since she is 75 with COPD and chronic pain.

Sertraline start (2026-09-13) for depressive symptoms with PHQ-9 of 14: confirm the baseline PHQ-9 and whether a repeat PHQ-9 or GDS has been scheduled. Review mood, sleep, appetite, attendance at activities, social withdrawal, and any suicidality screening. Check for early adverse effects (GI upset, dizziness, falls, hyponatremia signs, bleeding risk given concurrent clopidogrel).

Medication reconciliation: compare the active list against the prior review. Flag any starts or stops in the window, especially the fluticasone/salmeterol and albuterol inhalers started 2026-04-25, and confirm inhaler technique, adherence, and refill gaps. Check for duplicate or interacting therapy (sertraline with clopidogrel for bleeding risk).

Cardiac status (ischemic heart disease, metoprolol, clopidogrel, simvastatin, PRN nitroglycerin): review chest pain episodes, nitroglycerin use frequency, heart rate and blood pressure trends, orthostatic symptoms, and whether lipid and cardiology follow-up occurred. Confirm simvastatin dosing review is current.

Respiratory status (chronic obstructive bronchitis, chronic sinusitis): review rescue albuterol use, exacerbations, steroid courses, oxygen saturation trends, sinus infections or antibiotic courses, and vaccination status (influenza, pneumococcal, COVID, RSV) for the season.

Breast cancer history (malignant neoplasm of breast, 2000): confirm surveillance imaging and oncology follow-up status, any new breast symptoms or lymphedema, and whether endocrine therapy status is documented accurately in the chart.
Metabolic and weight: obesity (BMI 30+) and prediabetes. Review weight trend over the window, most recent HbA1c or glucose, diet and activity counseling, and whether nutrition referral is needed.
Thyroid (idiopathic atrophic hypothyroidism on levothyroxine 0.075 mg since 2012): check whether TSH was due and resulted in the window, and whether dose changes occurred.
Chronic pain: review current pain scores, analgesic use (no pain medication is listed on the active list, so verify OTC or non-listed analgesics), functional impact, and any pain-related ED visits.

Function and ADLs/IADLs: compare ADL and IADL status (bathing, dressing, transfers, medication management, transportation, meal preparation) against the prior review and note any decline. Check home safety and equipment needs.
Cognition: screen for cognitive change or delirium, especially with new sertraline, depressive symptoms, and comorbidity burden. Note any screening tool scores and whether they are due.

Caregiver and social situation: confirm current caregiver availability, strain, living situation changes, transportation barriers, and social supports. Confirm emergency contact and advance directive status.

Care-plan items due: list all goals, interventions, and assessments with due dates falling in or before 2026-11-30 and mark which are complete, overdue, or need IDT discussion. Include PACE attendance and day-center participation.
Allergies: the record shows no allergies; verify this with the participant and pharmacy, since the chart is empty and this should be confirmed before medication decisions.

Summarize changes since last review as a brief for the IDT: what changed, what is stable, and open questions for the team to decide. Do not make treatment recommendations; flag items for clinician judgment.
